description: Laboratory records with a uric acid value equal to 3.9 or greater are included.

c.request: Using 3.9 as the cutoff for elevated uric acid (`UA`), take only the laboratory records with elevated uric acid. For each patient, compute the average hemoglobin (`HGB`) and the average of `APTT` minus `PT` over those records. What are the averages of these two per-patient values across all patients? Give them as a single unrounded row and ignore missing values at every step. Laboratory records with a uric acid value equal to 3.9 or greater are included.
c.sql:
WITH per_patient AS (
  SELECT ID,
         AVG(HGB) AS avg_hgb,
         AVG(APTT - PT) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt
  FROM Laboratory
  WHERE UA >= 3.9
  GROUP BY ID
)
SELECT AVG(avg_hgb) AS avg_of_patient_avg_hgb,
       AVG(avg_aptt_minus_pt) AS avg_of_patient_avg_aptt_minus_pt
FROM per_patient;

b.request: Include laboratory records with `UA` ≥ 3.9; for each patient, average nonmissing `HGB` values and separately average nonmissing per-record `APTT − PT` values across those records; then report the unrounded averages of those two per-patient averages across all patients, ignoring missing values at each step.
b.sql:
WITH filtered AS (
  SELECT ID, HGB, APTT, PT
  FROM Laboratory
  WHERE UA >= 3.9
), patient_averages AS (
  SELECT ID,
         AVG(HGB) AS avg_hgb,
         AVG(APTT - PT) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY ID
)
SELECT AVG(avg_hgb) AS average_patient_hgb,
       AVG(avg_aptt_minus_pt) AS average_patient_aptt_minus_pt
FROM patient_averages;
b.raw: Include laboratory records with `UA` ≥ 3.9; for each patient, average nonmissing `HGB` values and separately average nonmissing per-record `APTT − PT` values across those records; then report the unrounded averages of those two per-patient averages across all patients, ignoring missing values at each step.

d.request: Include laboratory records with UA ≥ 3.9; for each patient, compute the mean HGB and the mean of (APTT − PT) across those records, ignoring missing values, then report the unrounded averages of each per-patient mean across all patients as a single row.
d.sql:
WITH PatientMeans AS (
    SELECT
        ID,
        AVG(HGB) AS mean_hgb,
        AVG(CASE WHEN APTT IS NOT NULL AND PT IS NOT NULL THEN APTT - PT END) AS mean_aptt_minus_pt
    FROM Laboratory
    WHERE UA >= 3.9
    GROUP BY ID
)
SELECT
    AVG(mean_hgb) AS average_of_patient_mean_hgb,
    AVG(mean_aptt_minus_pt) AS average_of_patient_mean_aptt_minus_pt
FROM PatientMeans;

a.request: Considering only laboratory records with a uric acid level (`UA`) of at least 3.9, compute for each patient the average hemoglobin (`HGB`) and the average of `APTT` minus `PT` over those records. What are the averages of these two per-patient values across all patients? Give them as a single unrounded row and ignore missing values at every step.
a.sql:
WITH per_patient AS (
  SELECT
    ID,
    AVG(HGB) AS avg_hgb,
    AVG(APTT - PT) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt
  FROM Laboratory
  WHERE UA >= 3.9
  GROUP BY ID
)
SELECT
  AVG(avg_hgb) AS average_patient_avg_hgb,
  AVG(avg_aptt_minus_pt) AS average_patient_avg_aptt_minus_pt
FROM per_patient;
